title: An alias key that names an earlier key is a duplicate however many keys lie between
notes: The alias `*a` is the node `foo` that the anchor names (YAML 1.2.2 section 7.1), so the mapping holds the key `foo` twice, which section 3.2.1.1 forbids. Forty other keys lie between the two, a size at which a reader that checks keys cheaply in small mappings might switch to another way of comparing.

provenance.reference: Differential testing of the oneyaml-python native and pure backends; both backends refuse this document when it is loaded as data; the pure backend accepted it when it read it for editing (`edit/patch-of-a-document-with-a-duplicate-key-through-an-alias-key-is-refused`).
